ANNUAL MULTI-TRIP TRAVEL COVER
Issued by Meridian Travel Insurance Ltd

1. Definitions
1.1. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
1.3. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.4. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.5. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.6. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.7. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.8. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Emergency Medical Expenses
3.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
4.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
5.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

7. Making a claim
7.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.2. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

8. Records and evidence
8.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
8.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
8.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

9. Interest
9.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

10. Cancellation
10.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
10.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
10.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

11. Assignment
11.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

12. Personal liability
12.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
12.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
12.3. The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

13. Emergency assistance
13.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
13.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
13.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

14. Severability
14.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

15. Renewal
15.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
15.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

16. Arbitration
16.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
16.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

17. Environmental commitment
17.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
17.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

18. Customer support
18.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
18.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

19. Legal expenses abroad
19.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
19.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

20. Geographical limits
20.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
20.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

21. Cooperation
21.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
21.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

22. Third-party administrators
22.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
22.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

23. Accessibility
23.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

24. Recovery of costs
24.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

25. Discounts
25.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
25.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

5.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
5.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
5.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
5.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

6. Optional cover: Hearing Care
6.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
6.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $100 per treatment.
6.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.5. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

8. Making a claim
8.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.3. You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

9. Geographical limits
9.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
9.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

10. Market conditions
10.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

11. Interest
11.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

12. Accessibility
12.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

13. Reasonable precautions
13.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
13.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

14. Claims documents
14.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
14.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

15. Discounts
15.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
15.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

16. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
16.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

17. Assignment
17.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

18. Taxes
18.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
18.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

19. Complaints
19.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
19.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
19.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

20. Notices
20.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
20.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

21. Electronic documents
21.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
21.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
21.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

22. Sanctions
22.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

23. Governing law
23.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
23.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

24. Coordination of benefits
24.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
24.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

25. Fraud
25.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
25.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

26. Compensation scheme
26.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
26.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

27. Environmental commitment
27.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
27.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

28. Cancellation
28.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
28.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
28.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

29. Eligibility
29.1. Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
29.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

30. Arbitration
30.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
30.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

31. Recovery of costs
31.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

32. Payment of claims
32.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
32.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

33. Currency
33.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
33.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

34. Wellness allowance
34.1. Each plan year you may claim up to $250 towards a gym membership or fitness class.
34.2. The wellness allowance is not subject to any deductible and does not count towards other limits.

35. Other insurance
35.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
35.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

36. Inflation
36.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
36.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

37. Automatic renewal
37.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
37.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

38. Change of address
38.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
38.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

39. Subrogation
39.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
39.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

40. Waiver
40.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

41. Communication
41.1. We will communicate with you in English.
41.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

42. Customer support
42.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
42.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

43. Appeals
43.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
43.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
43.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

44. Severability
44.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

45. Salvage
45.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
45.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

46. Cooperation
46.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
46.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

47. Duty of fair presentation
47.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
47.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
47.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

48. Joint policyholders
48.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
48.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

49. Renewal
49.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
49.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

50. Instalment agreements
50.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
50.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

51. Premium payment
51.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
51.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

52. Dependants
52.1. You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
52.2. Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

53. Leaving the plan
53.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
53.2. Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

54. Records and evidence
54.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
54.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
54.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

55. Interpretation
55.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
55.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
55.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

56. Third-party administrators
56.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
56.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

57. Changes in circumstances
57.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
57.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

58. Exchange of information
58.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
58.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

59. Data protection
59.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
59.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
59.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

60. How to read this document
60.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
60.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
60.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

1. Definitions
1.1. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.3. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.4. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.5. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.6. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
1.7. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.8. Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with you on the same trip.
1.9. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Emergency Medical Expenses
3.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
3.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
4.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

5. General exclusions
5.1. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
5.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

6. Making a claim
6.1. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
6.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
6.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

7. Repatriation
7.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
7.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

8. Electronic documents
8.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
8.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
8.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

9. Environmental commitment
9.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
9.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

10. Arbitration
10.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
10.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

11. Reasonable precautions
11.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
11.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

12. Payment of claims
12.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
12.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

13. Assignment
13.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

14. Instalment agreements
14.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
14.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

1.2. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.3. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.6. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.8. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.9. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
1.10. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.11. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.12. Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.13. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
1.14. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.15. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.16. Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.17. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Trip Cancellation
3.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
3.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

4. Emergency Medical Expenses
4.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
4.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
4.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

5. Baggage and Personal Belongings
5.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
5.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
5.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
5.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
5.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

6. Optional cover: Travel Delay
6.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
6.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
7.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
7.4. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

8. Making a claim
8.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
8.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.3. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

9. Inflation
9.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
9.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

10. Interest
10.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

11. Complaints
11.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
11.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
11.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

12. Other insurance
12.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
12.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

13. Market conditions
13.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

14. Communication
14.1. We will communicate with you in English.
14.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

15. Arbitration
15.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
15.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

16. Rental car excess
16.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
16.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

17. Third-party administrators
17.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
17.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

18. Exchange of information
18.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
18.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

19. Environmental commitment
19.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
19.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

20. Renewal
20.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
20.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

21. Repatriation
21.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
21.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

22. Cancellation
22.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
22.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
22.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

23. Changes in circumstances
23.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
23.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

24. Claims documents
24.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
24.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

25. Assignment
25.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

26. How to read this document
26.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
26.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
26.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

27. Cooperation
27.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
27.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

28. Personal liability
28.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
28.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
28.3. The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

29. Taxes
29.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
29.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

30. Geographical limits
30.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
30.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

31. Notices
31.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
31.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

32. Duty of fair presentation
32.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
32.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
32.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

33. Data protection
33.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
33.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
33.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

34. Salvage
34.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
34.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

35. Fraud
35.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
35.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

36. Governing law
36.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
36.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

37. Instalment agreements
37.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
37.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

38. Joint policyholders
38.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
38.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

39. Currency
39.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
39.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

27. Taxes
27.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
27.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

28. Cancellation
28.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
28.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
28.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

29. Instalment agreements
29.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
29.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

30. Optional cover: Travel Delay
30.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
30.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
30.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

31. Currency
31.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
31.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

32. Data protection
32.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
32.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
32.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

33. Rental car excess
33.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
33.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

34. Governing law
34.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
34.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

35. Baggage and Personal Belongings
35.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
35.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
35.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
35.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
35.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
35.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

36. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
36.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

37. Emergency Medical Expenses
37.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
37.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
37.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
37.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
37.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
37.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

38. How to read this document
38.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
38.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
38.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

39. Claims documents
39.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
39.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

40. Electronic documents
40.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
40.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
40.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

41. Duty of fair presentation
41.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
41.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
41.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

42. Communication
42.1. We will communicate with you in English.
42.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

43. Fraud
43.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
43.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

44. Missed departure
44.1. We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
44.2. You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

45. Compensation scheme
45.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
45.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

46. Interpretation
46.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
46.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
46.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

47. Interest
47.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

48. Automatic renewal
48.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
48.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

49. Assignment
49.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

50. Discounts
50.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
50.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

51. Repatriation
51.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
51.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

52. Emergency assistance
52.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
52.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
52.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

53. Exchange of information
53.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
53.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

54. General exclusions
54.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
54.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
54.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
54.4. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
54.5. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
54.6. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

55. Making a claim
55.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
55.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
55.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

56. Customer support
56.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
56.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

57. Records and evidence
57.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
57.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
57.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

58. Third-party administrators
58.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
58.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

59. Changes in circumstances
59.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
59.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

60. Accessibility

ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Brightline Device Cover

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.4. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.5. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.6. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.7. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.8. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.9. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.10. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.11. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.12. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Breakdown
3.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
3.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

4. Communication
4.1. We will communicate with you in English.
4.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

5. Cooperation
5.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
5.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

6. Transferring the plan
6.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
6.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

7. Assignment
7.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

8. Governing law
8.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
8.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

9. Data protection
9.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
9.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
9.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

10. Interpretation
10.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
10.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
10.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

11. Instalment agreements
11.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
11.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

12. Waiver
12.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

13. Accidental Damage
13.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
13.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
13.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.

1) Outages propagate along hard dependencies: if a service goes down, every service that depends on it, directly or through other hard dependencies, is affected. Soft dependencies do not propagate outages.
2) payments-gateway depends on session-cache.
3) session-cache depends on email-relay.
4) auth-service depends on email-relay.
5) billing-api depends on notification-hub.
6) order-queue depends on fraud-scorer.

1. Definitions

1.5. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
1.6. Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.7. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.

2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.

2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Emergency Medical Expenses
3.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
3.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
3.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
3.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
3.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

4. Baggage and Personal Belongings
4.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
4.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $450 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
4.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

5. General exclusions
5.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
5.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
5.3. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

6. Making a claim
6.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
6.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
6.3. You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

7.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
7.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

8.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
8.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
8.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

9. Sanctions
9.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

10. Geographical limits
10.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
10.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

11. Currency
11.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
11.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

12. Emergency assistance
12.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
12.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
12.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

13. Notices
13.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
13.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

14. Communication

14.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

15. Inflation

15.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

18.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

19.3. The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

21. Interest

22.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
22.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

23.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
23.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

24. Governing law

24.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

25. Salvage
25.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
25.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

26. Subrogation
26.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
26.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

27. Other insurance
27.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
27.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

28. Waiver
28.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

29. Renewal

30.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
30.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
30.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

31. Customer support
31.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
31.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

32. Change of address
32.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
32.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

33. Environmental commitment
33.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
33.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

34. Third-party administrators
34.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
34.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

35. Inflation
35.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
35.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

36. Premium payment
36.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
36.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

37. Other insurance
37.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
37.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

38. Automatic renewal
38.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
38.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

39. Salvage
39.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
39.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

40. Exchange of information
40.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
40.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

41. Electronic documents
41.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
41.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
41.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

42. Transferring the plan
42.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
42.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

43. Market conditions
43.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

44. Assignment
44.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

45. Geographical limits
45.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
45.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

46. Making a claim
46.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
46.2. You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
46.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

47. Software support
47.1. Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
47.2. Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

48. Sanctions
48.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

49. Cancellation
49.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
49.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
49.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

50. Compensation scheme
50.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
50.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

51. Replacement devices
51.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
51.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
51.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

52. Instalment agreements
52.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
52.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

53. Changes in circumstances
53.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
53.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

54. Unrecoverable devices
54.1. If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
54.2. We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

55. Currency
55.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
55.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

56. Notices
56.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
56.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

57. Interest
57.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

58. Complaints
58.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
58.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
58.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

59. Claims documents
59.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
59.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Keystone Home Mutual

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.3. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.4. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.5. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Escape of Water
3.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
3.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
3.3. We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
3.4. We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

4. Flood
4.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
4.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
4.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
5.1. We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
5.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

7. Making a claim
7.1. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
7.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

8. Recovery of costs
8.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

9. Locks and keys
9.1. If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
9.2. The most we will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

10. Reasonable precautions
10.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
10.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

11. Other insurance
11.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
11.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

12. Cooperation
12.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
12.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

13. Governing law
13.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
13.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

14. Fraud
14.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
14.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

15. Automatic renewal
15.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
15.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

16. Environmental commitment
16.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
16.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

17. Claims documents
17.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
17.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

For the past couple of years thoughts of self harm and suicide have come and gone, even when I was in a really great place in life. Recently(the past few months) things have gotten worse for me. Multiple factors are piling up and it's starting to feel like it's entirely too much to handle. This past weekend I stayed at my ex's house and tonight when I got home something just changed, got worse somehow, and I just wanted to end it. I was actually going to do it. For some reason though, I spoke to him and he talked me out of it before he had to go to bed(he has school today), he wants me to get help but I can't afford to get any. He told me that he might "turn me in" which I think means tell someone at his school or the police or something about what I've been thinking of. I told him I'd never forgive him, and I can't handle my parents reactions if he did tell someone, but deep down I would give anything to have some help. I've told him for over a year now that I need help and I think he's just now starting to believe me. He told me he will get me help no matter what, but I'm so afraid of some authority figure finding out what I've been thinking of doing. I can't even talk to anyone face to face about it. I can barely talk to anybody about anything face to face. I'm not sure if I have social anxiety(the talking to people/being around people part), depression, both, or neither but I'm sure that I'm sick of my life being this way. I'm sick of existing and not living. I found this subreddit through MMFB(which I found through IAMA), and I just had to let it out somewhere where my face was unknown. I don't know if you've read this far, but if you have thank you. If you care for me to, I can try to keep this updated.
Also, in case someone was wondering why I don't go to another friend for help instead of my ex, it's because my ex is literally the only friend I have. I had a clique that we both hung out with but I(stupidly) pushed them away.

+            )
